requirement:
A provider failure that ends the model conversation returns
`ValidationError::Provider` with the underlying I/O error to the awaiting ask builder.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.tool_agent.provider_failure` is: "A provider failure that ends the model conversation returns `ValidationError::Provider` with the underlying I/O error to the awaiting ask builder." It states observable behavior only, so it creates no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence.

I checked each clause that might be structural:
- **"`ValidationError::Provider` with the underlying I/O error".** This names the value the awaiting caller gets. A different design could change the internals and still hand the caller `Err(ValidationError::Provider(io_error))`. That design would satisfy the text, so the internals are discretionary. The declaration of the `ValidationError` enum belongs to a separate requirement, `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ValidationError`. It is not prescribed here.
- **"returns ... to the awaiting ask builder".** This describes what the caller observes from awaiting `ask`. It does not prescribe delegation through a named interface. The current code happens to map `AgentError::Provider` to `ValidationError::Provider` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[Ask<'a, 'd, D, R, P>]#2/fn[execute]`, with `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent.rs#fn[converse]` producing `AgentError::Provider`. A different internal error path could return the same result, so that route is not required.

No implementation roots were supplied, and none is needed. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

behavioral: The requirement has one behavioral obligation. When a provider failure ends the model conversation, the awaiting ask builder gets `ValidationError::Provider` that carries the underlying I/O error.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]` covers the main scenario. `Script::new(vec![None])` makes `Script/CompletionProvider::complete` return `io::Error::other("permanent provider failure")`. The test awaits `ctx.ask::<bool>()` and asserts `Err(ValidationError::Provider(error))` with `error.to_string()` containing "permanent provider failure". That checks both the variant and that the underlying I/O error's message is preserved. It also asserts `ctx.dependencies().is_empty()`, which shows no result was produced. The same test's text-only scenario returns `ValidationError::Agent`, so a provider failure is distinguished from a missing submission.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]` adds a second provider-failure path. A missing credential fails the awaited ask with `ValidationError::Provider`, and the message names the credential variable. The test also checks the deterministic question is unaffected, because only the awaited ask is affected.

The tests only fail the first request. A failure after earlier tool-call turns is not exercised. The requirement does not distinguish failures by turn, so I don't count this as a gap. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there are no marking gaps.
